name: Ben Allen

education.notes: BSc Computer Science confirmed via multiple secondary sources; exact graduation year not pinned down from public sources.

keyDecisions: Took a software engineering role in transportation / intelligent traffic systems straight after Bristol, rather than going into a big bank or consultancy
lessons: Working on hard-real-world systems (transport infrastructure) early teaches you to ship to constraints that pure web SaaS never enforces
careerSteps.notes: Q-Free is a Norwegian-headquartered intelligent transport systems company; Ben worked on AI-adjacent software for transportation.

keyDecisions: Moved from transport software into robotics / AI software at Dyson — pattern of seeking hard technical problems before B2B SaaS
lessons: Hardware-adjacent engineering forces deep ownership: there is no 'just push a hotfix' when your code touches physical things
careerSteps.notes: Worked on AI software for Dyson's robotics arm before pivoting into pure software / B2B SaaS.

keyDecisions: First founder attempt before Omnea — built and ran product / engineering teams as CTO
lessons: A first founding experience (even sub-scale) is the cheapest tuition for the second one — you learn what 'CTO' actually means in practice
careerSteps.notes: Drove Canary & Delta to seven-figure revenue and built / managed the product and engineering teams; an underrated pre-Tessian founder reps cycle.

keyDecisions: Joined Tessian during its scale-up phase as a senior technical leader
Left Tessian in 2021 to start Omnea via Entrepreneur First with Ben Freeman, ahead of the Proofpoint acquisition
lessons: An operator role at a Sequoia/Accel-backed UK scale-up is a fast credibility track for raising tier-1 capital on the next venture
Selling into enterprise from the vendor side teaches you firsthand how broken procurement is — the seed of Omnea's thesis
careerSteps.notes: Tessian (UK email security) raised $130M+ from Sequoia, Accel, Balderton and others; acquired by Proofpoint in 2023. Ben Allen and Ben Freeman were both Tessian alumni.

keyDecisions: Co-founded Omnea via Entrepreneur First (EF) with Ben Freeman, having met him through the Tessian alumni network
Bet on procurement orchestration as a horizontal, AI-native category rather than a point solution
Built engineering org with a hard talent-density bar (~10,500 interviews for first ~45 hires across the company)
lessons: Vertical SaaS works best when founders have lived the customer pain (procurement seen from the vendor side at Tessian)
EF can be a credible launchpad for technical co-founders in the UK who lack a pre-existing co-founder
Pairing a technical co-founder with a hustler-operator CEO (Freeman) shortens the path to enterprise revenue
careerSteps.notes: Omnea: AI-native intake/orchestration platform for enterprise procurement. ~150 staff (London + NY) by late 2025. Backed by Accel, Khosla, Insight, Point Nine, First Round, Prosus. Customers include Spotify, Wise, MongoDB, Adecco, Albertsons. Ranked #1 in Startups 100 2026.

outcomes.currentStatus: Co-founder & CTO of Omnea (London/NY). Omnea has raised ~$75M cumulative (Seed, $20M Series A, $50M Series B in Sep 2025 led by Insight Partners and Khosla Ventures). Ranked #1 in Startups 100 2026.

lessons.lesson: Hardware/AI-adjacent engineering jobs (Q-Free, Dyson) before B2B SaaS build a technical depth that pure-web CTOs often lack.
A sub-scale first founding attempt (Canary & Delta) is cheap tuition for the second, VC-backed one.
Operator-to-founder: deep operator experience at a scale-up (Tessian) gave both Bens credibility to raise from tier-1 VCs.
EF is a viable route for UK technical founders without an existing co-founder.
